recipes.name: Marinated Rib-Eyes
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon garlic powder, or to taste
1 teaspoon onion powder, or to taste

steps.text: Season steaks with garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper; set aside.

Place Worcestershire sauce and brown sugar into a large resealable plastic bag; seal the bag and shake to mix. Pour 1/2 of the marinade into another large resealable plastic bag. Place 2 steaks in each bag and turn to coat. Squeeze out excess air and seal the bags. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Preheat an outdoor grill for high heat and lightly oil the grate.
Drain marinade from the bags into a small saucepan; bring to a boil and cook for 3 to 4 minutes. Set aside.

Grill steaks on the preheated grill to desired doneness, about 7 minutes per side. Baste often with boiled marinade during the final 5 minutes of cook time. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of steaks should read 140 degrees F (60 degrees C) for medium doneness.

raw_recipe.headline: Marinated Rib-Eyes
raw_recipe.description: Marinating rib-eye steaks in a savory mixture of Worcestershire, brown sugar, garlic, and onion adds incredible flavor to these grilled steaks.

review.reviewBody: A tad too sweet for me. We like some other marinades better, but this was good.

I didn't make a change to the recipe itself. But instead of grilling I pan fried. Used butter of course. With the butter & not adding any marinade this was absolutely delicious. This is a keeper in this household.

i loved this marinade, i reduced the brown sugar to about 1/4 a cup instead of a 3rd, and added about half a tablespoon of sriracha to add some heat. the sweetness to heat really did me in. pairing this with scalloped potatoes and sauteed veggies was a great meal.

This was so tender and flavorful. The best steak I've ever had hands down. We decreased the brown sugar a bit after reading the reviews and I think that was a wise choice. We will be making these again I'm sure. Even the kids loved this one.
This was pretty good. I added rosemary and minced garlic to it for a more exciting fresh taste.

I actually will make it again... I didn't have all of the Worcestershire sauce required so I used beef broth to actually balance it out.... but it still came out tender and delicious. Also my fiancé could actually eat it. He takes his dentures out so that he can actually eat steak and normally when he does that he cant eat... but he could with these and he had a whole pound steak gone in like 5 minutes. Thanks for the great recipe.

This was awesome, the brown sugar adds a nice char. I only added a teaspoon of Trader Joes Garlic Aioli Mustard to each bag and it really deepened the flavor. Will use this as a go to marinade from now on

Delicious! I think next time i will keep some of the marinade before i add the meat for basting since i cooked it with a frying pan. It wasn't greasy since i browned the steaks on high first and then let the meat cook with the marinade. Yummy!

This was my first time making a homemade marinade.... it was not difficult at all! My husband & I LOVED it! I used spicy brown mustard and it added a little bit of heat which was nice but not over powering. We were very pleased with this recipe! :0)

This was absolutely delicious! I was very surprised at how wonderful it turned out. I was worried that it would come out as too sweet, but it was perfect! I was looking for a different way to marinate my steaks because I was getting bored with the usual. I am so glad I came across this one! The ONLY things I did were halved the recipe for two rib-eye steaks and used Tony Cachere's seasoning instead of salt for just a little extra flavor. I will definitely be using this recipe again!

I've used the recipe several times. My picky girlfriend who's not a steak lover enjoyed the steaks. She will only eat well done, so after I used the high heat to sear the meat, I moved the steaks to a medium heat to allow it to get a little more tender. Takes longer, but doesn't dry it out as much.
The marinade was just right! I topped the steaks with a gorgonzola sauce. The steaks were a hit!
Followed recipe exactly then cooked in the air fryer. Delicious
Love this recipe, the brown sugar makes it a bit sweet so after I cooked the steaks I had to add a little more salt to the steaks.
Was not a fan of the flavor. It was different but not good to me or husband.
SOOOOO GOOOD
Very tender and flavorful. My new go-to marinade.
We made this exactly and those were the best Rib Eyes that we have had in a long time! Will make again very soon! Thank you to whoever came up with this recipe! It's a Winner!!!!!!!!!

FANTASTIC! I have been grilling steaks for decades, many different marinades or none at all. Great compliments from guests previously, but these are the BEST ribeyes I have ever cooked or tasted outside of a 5 star restaurant!!!

This is one of the worst marinades I have used for meat. The Worcester is overpowering and the steak inedible when cooked. I had and extra piece of meat and did not want to waste it. I Threw away the marinade and soaked the meat in water.
